about.title: About
lines: Wikimedia publishes how often every Wikipedia article is read, every hour.
Looked Up reads the 30 largest editions, which carry 98.5 % of human article views.
Each article is compared with its own last 28 days at the same hour.
A spike is a sudden jump far above that baseline.
Wikidata joins the same topic across languages, so Lisbon, Lisboa and リスボン count as one.
An event is one topic spiking in two languages or more within six hours.
Tiers say how far it spread: noticed (2+), international (5+), planetary (20+).
It updates every hour, about three hours behind real time, because that is when the data is published.
limits: Delay: Wikimedia publishes each hour about two hours after it ends, so the newest events are about three hours old.
Languages, not countries: a spike in Spanish could come from Mexico, Spain or the United States.
Fame bias: widely known people and spectacles spread; local news rarely leaves its language.
30 languages: they carry 98.5 % of human views, but entire communities beyond them are invisible here.
